document.title: Message to the Taliban on Bin Laden (State 154713)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret (NODIS)] Apparent response to Mullah Omar's request for evidence. It outlines the justification for the U.S. strikes, the case against bin Laden, and grounds for his expulsion. It cites 'reliable intelligence' that the bin Laden network sought weapons of mass destruction, including chemical weapons, and had tried to blow up U.S. airliners in the Pacific.

sources_cited: Reftel: record of telephone conversation with Mullah Omar, 22 Aug 1998
key_claims: The US sought to engage the Taliban through the Islamabad embassy to secure bin Laden's expulsion after the Khowst and Khartoum strikes.
The US asserts the Khowst bases serve multiple groups tied to the bin Laden network for refuge, funding, travel and training.
The US claims the bin Laden network is seeking chemical weapons and other WMD.
The US argues bin Laden violates Pushtunwali hospitality by launching attacks from Afghan soil.
The US acknowledges Taliban attempts to control bin Laden failed and that dialogue may be a ploy for recognition or stalling.
